beats: Hook: with 23 people in a room it is more likely than not that two share a birthday (her framing, Q25-09 54:47-56:36; 50.7%: check in FACTS.md): line_qc_simon_birthday_party. Simon's problem is a birthday hunt over 2^n days: a classical search needs about 2^(n/2) tries, a quantum computer about n runs. Same cast as QC07-05: the sleuth and the host (cast drawing line_qc_onequery_two_cabinets).
Beyond exact values, a hidden periodicity (48:54-51:07; clip 49:21-50:12: periodicity, then the Fourier transform, then Shor): line_qc_simon_wallpaper (find the repeat of the pattern).

The problem (51:43-53:34): f(x1) = f(x2) exactly when x2 = x1 xor s, so every output is shared by exactly one pair, like a basket in which every sock has exactly one twin (line_qc_simon_sock_basket; reuse line_paired_cards); find s.

Classically, pull socks until two match (53:34-56:36): a birthday hunt, about 2^(n/2) queries (Simon 1994, lower bound Omega(2^(n/2)): check in FACTS.md); her 23-people version, back to line_qc_simon_birthday_party.
The circuit (56:49-59:25): H, the oracle into a second register, measure that register, H, measure; code draws it (tape Q25-09 s42).

Each run returns a random y with y.s = 0 (59:37-70:44; clip 70:21-70:44, "you immediately know that y times s equals zero"): one clue, which rules out half of the candidates for s (line_qc_simon_flip_board).

Collect n-1 independent clues and solve the linear equations: about n runs in expectation (70:45-75:11; her 4(n-1) bound is loose: use the standard statement; tape Q25-09 s50): line_qc_simon_clue_board; clip 75:11-75:36, "much better results". Code draws n against 2^(n/2).

Where it led: the quantum Fourier transform and Shor's factoring algorithm (Shor 1994), the problem much of today's encryption rests on (keep it at that): line_qc_simon_stepping_stones (Deutsch-Jozsa, Bernstein-Vazirani, Simon, then the big lock on the far bank); reuse line_qc_perfect_special_key (QC01-02).
Cover (line_qc_cover_07_06; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the sleuth sits by an overflowing sock basket holding up two matching socks; the host leans in, impressed.
